passages.text: We are living in the midst of such a mass of miracles, day and night, that we do not think anything of them.
passages.note: Taking everyday wonders for granted; gratitude

passages.text: The water for irrigation of fields is already in the canal, only shut in by gates. The farmer opens these gates, and the water flows in by itself, by the law of gravitation. So all progress and power are already in every man; perfection is man’s nature, only it is barred in and prevented from taking its proper course. If anyone can take the bar off, in rushes nature.
passages.note: Self-doubt; potential already within, only blocked

passages.text: Whatever you do never destroys your own glory, your own nature, because the soul cannot be acted upon by anything, only a veil is spread before it, hiding its perfection.
passages.note: Guilt over past deeds; inner worth remains intact
